    31|def _get_service_pids() -> set:
    32|    """Return PIDs currently managed by systemd or launchd gateway services.
    33|
    34|    Used to avoid killing freshly-restarted service processes when sweeping
    35|    for stale manual gateway processes after a service restart.  Relies on the
    36|    service manager having committed the new PID before the restart command
    37|    returns (true for both systemd and launchd in practice).
    38|    """
    39|    pids: set = set()
    40|
    41|    # --- systemd (Linux): user and system scopes ---
    42|    if is_linux():
    43|        for scope_args in [["systemctl", "--user"], ["systemctl"]]:
    44|            try:
    45|                result = subprocess.run(
    46|                    scope_args + ["list-units", "hermes-gateway*",
    47|                                  "--plain", "--no-legend", "--no-pager"],
    48|                    capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
    49|                )
    50|                for line in result.stdout.strip().splitlines():
    51|                    parts = line.split()
    52|                    if not parts or not parts[0].endswith(".service"):
    53|                        continue
    54|                    svc = parts[0]
    55|                    try:
    56|                        show = subprocess.run(
    57|                            scope_args + ["show", svc,
    58|                                          "--property=MainPID", "--value"],
    59|                            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
    60|                        )
    61|                        pid = int(show.stdout.strip())
    62|                        if pid > 0:
    63|                            pids.add(pid)
    64|                    except (ValueError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
    65|                        pass
    66|            except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
    67|                pass
    68|
    69|    # --- launchd (macOS) ---
    70|    if is_macos():
    71|        try:
    72|            label = get_launchd_label()
    73|            result = subprocess.run(
    74|                ["launchctl", "list", label],
    75|                capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
    76|            )
    77|            if result.returncode == 0:
    78|                # Output: "PID\tStatus\tLabel" header, then one data line
    79|                for line in result.stdout.strip().splitlines():
    80|                    parts = line.split()
    81|                    if len(parts) >= 3 and parts[2] == label:
    82|                        try:
    83|                            pid = int(parts[0])

    88|        except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):

    94|def find_gateway_pids(exclude_pids: set | None = None) -> list:
    95|    """Find PIDs of running gateway processes.
    96|
    97|    Args:
    98|        exclude_pids: PIDs to exclude from the result (e.g. service-managed
    99|            PIDs that should not be killed during a stale-process sweep).
   100|    """
   101|    pids = []
   102|    _exclude = exclude_pids or set()
   103|    patterns = [
   104|        "hermes_cli.main gateway",
   105|        "hermes_cli/main.py gateway",
   106|        "hermes gateway",
   107|        "gateway/run.py",
   108|    ]
   109|
   110|    try:
   111|        if is_windows():
   112|            # Windows: use wmic to search command lines
   113|            result = subprocess.run(
   114|                ["wmic", "process", "get", "ProcessId,CommandLine", "/FORMAT:LIST"],
   115|                capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10
   116|            )
   117|            # Parse WMIC LIST output: blocks of "CommandLine=...\nProcessId=...\n"
   118|            current_cmd = ""
   119|            for line in result.stdout.split('\n'):
   120|                line = line.strip()
   121|                if line.startswith("CommandLine="):
   122|                    current_cmd = line[len("CommandLine="):]
   123|                elif line.startswith("ProcessId="):
   124|                    pid_str = line[len("ProcessId="):]
   125|                    if any(p in current_cmd for p in patterns):
   126|                        try:
   127|                            pid = int(pid_str)
   128|                            if pid != os.getpid() and pid not in pids and pid not in _exclude:
   129|                                pids.append(pid)
   130|                        except ValueError:
   131|                            pass
   132|                    current_cmd = ""
   133|        else:
   134|            result = subprocess.run(
   135|                ["ps", "aux"],
   136|                capture_output=True,
   137|                text=True,
   138|                timeout=10,
   139|            )
   140|            for line in result.stdout.split('\n'):
   141|                # Skip grep and current process
   142|                if 'grep' in line or str(os.getpid()) in line:
   143|                    continue
   144|                for pattern in patterns:
   145|                    if pattern in line:
   146|                        parts = line.split()
   147|                        if len(parts) > 1:
   148|                            try:
   149|                                pid = int(parts[1])
   150|                                if pid not in pids and pid not in _exclude:
   151|                                    pids.append(pid)
   152|                            except ValueError:
   153|                                continue
   154|                        break
   155|    except Exception:
   156|        pass
   157|
   158|    return pids

   161|def kill_gateway_processes(force: bool = False, exclude_pids: set | None = None) -> int:
   162|    """Kill any running gateway processes. Returns count killed.
   163|
   164|    Args:
   165|        force: Use SIGKILL instead of SIGTERM.
   166|        exclude_pids: PIDs to skip (e.g. service-managed PIDs that were just
   167|            restarted and should not be killed).
   168|    """
   169|    pids = find_gateway_pids(exclude_pids=exclude_pids)
   170|    killed = 0
   171|    
   172|    for pid in pids:
   173|        try:
   174|            if force and not is_windows():
   175|                os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
   176|            else:

   179|        except ProcessLookupError:

   182|        except PermissionError:

   243|def _profile_suffix() -> str:
   244|    """Derive a service-name suffix from the current HERMES_HOME.
   245|
   246|    Returns ``""`` for the default ``~/.hermes``, the profile name for
   247|    ``~/.hermes/profiles/<name>``, or a short hash for any other custom
   248|    HERMES_HOME path.
   249|    """
   250|    import hashlib
   251|    import re
   252|    from pathlib import Path as _Path
   253|    home = get_hermes_home().resolve()
   254|    default = (_Path.home() / ".hermes").resolve()
   255|    if home == default:
   256|        return ""
   257|    # Detect ~/.hermes/profiles/<name> pattern → use the profile name
   258|    profiles_root = (default / "profiles").resolve()
   259|    try:
   260|        rel = home.relative_to(profiles_root)
   261|        parts = rel.parts
   262|        if len(parts) == 1 and re.match(r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$", parts[0]):
   263|            return parts[0]
   264|    except ValueError:

   267|    return hashlib.sha256(str(home).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
